title.narrative: NIHR Global Health Research Cohort Academic Development Award - GHR CADA 2023

description.narrative:
The NIHR GHR Cohort Academic Development Award (GHR CADA) scheme offers NIHR GHR Programme Training Leads (or Directors/Principle investigators (PIs) where there is no training lead in place) an opportunity to tailor a programme of activities to meet the academic training and career development needs of the cohort of NIHR GHR Academy members in their NIHR GHR Programme awards (primarily focussed on those who are LMIC based) and, where training needs align, with other NIHR GHR Programme awards.
Individuals can apply to the GHR CADA scheme for up to £30,000 to undertake a programme of activities. Applications are light-touch and will be assessed in an open competition. Funding can include training course fees, invited speaker or facilitator costs, accommodation, travel, subsistence and any other reasonable expenses, for example internet connectivity costs incurred during the activities.
Following completion of a GHR CADA award, the awardee is expected to be able to show evidence of:
Completion of the programme of activities proposed in the application Development of new research or technical skills/techniques within the cohort Increased academic career development of the cohort Involvement in collaborative relationships and increased networks. Evidence of the above will be sought by the NIHR through the GHR CADA final report.
These guidance notes are intended to help completion of an application for the NIHR GHR CADA, Round 2 (2022). The NIHR Academy office can be contacted with any eligibility queries. Please contact the NIHR with any eligibility queries (ghrtp@nihr.ac.uk).

activity-date.narrative: Lead by Dr. Abrudan, this training programme is set to focus on the emerging field of Digital Epidemiology. Dr Abrudan is the Training Development Lead for the Centre for Genomic Pathogen Surveillance. This programme will be organised in coordination with the Global Health Research Unit project, also being coordinated by CGPS and funded by the NIHR, for the lead PIs and scientists to assist in the fight against antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

recipient-country.narrative: The GHR CADA funding will be wholly received by the University of Oxford in conjunction with the global health research unit (GHRU) project. The funding will provide a financial basis for a workshop that will be ran by CGPS for the wider GHRU team. This includes our collaborators from Colombia (Corporación colombiana de investigación agropecuaria - AGROSAVIA), Nigeria (University of Ibadan), India (Kempegowda Institute of Medical Sciences - KIMS), and the Philippines (Research Institute for Tropical Medicine - RITM).

sector.narrative: GHR CADA funding is committed in conjunction with the Global Health Research Unit project. This workshop funding will go towards the emerging digital epidemiology practices to reinforce the GHRU project.
